correctness.rationale: Proof explicitly derives operator entries from minima of relation rows and their last occurrences; adjacent upset inputs recover each occurrence coordinate. This yields an injective invariant and a canonical graph with k edges; any other relation needs k distinct nonempty rows, giving uniqueness at equality. Counting partial injections gives rank polynomial and total, and independent weighted row choices yield exact raw-relation fibres. Boundary cases n=1, empty rows, absent labels and p>=q are treated. Running the attached scripts checked all raw relations n<=4 and all upward-flat threshold relations n<=6, with finite computation used solely as support for the all-n argument.

originality.rationale: Comparisons are by mathematical implication. The foundational 2026 paper supplies the flat clause and upward-target closure but neither the last-occurrence bijection nor the unique minimum-edge representative. General weak Heyting counting is a broader algebraic classification, not equivalent to this restricted relational representation; the three-element chain has 9 weak Heyting operations versus 7 flat-representable operations. The rank sequence is known (OEIS A002720/A144084) and is not claimed as novel. The 2015 full text remains unread and carries a specific residual specialization risk. No exact or dominating theorem emerged from published-claim, alias, source and database searches.
residual_risks: The full text of Alizadeh–Joharizadeh (2015) was inaccessible; its detailed algorithms may contain a chain-specific special case not visible in the abstract.
An equivalent minimal-graph correspondence could be indexed under inverse semigroups, strict-implication duality, or finite chain relation quotients without the same terminology.
Searches and local files cannot establish universal novelty, and unpublished external work is not visible.

value.rationale: A natural and previously unclassified structural problem raised by the 2026 flat semantics is how many distinct implication operations relational models produce and how economically they can be represented. On all finite chains, the theorem supplies one unique optimal relation for every operator, an intrinsic minimal-arrow complexity rank, a complete isomorphism classification, and exact redundancy fibres among all raw relations. These are substantive exact normal-form results across all sizes, beyond a table of examples or a known sequence identity; they apply directly to relational-model minimization and semantic-equivalence testing.
